column3: The Hebrew says “after days” and calls the room “the chamber”; BSB has “Later on” and “her room”.
The Hebrew calls him “your companion” in the singular, not explicitly “one of the men who accompanied you”. The comparison is “better”, rather than explicitly “more beautiful”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he turned tail to tail and placed a torch between the two tails; it does not explicitly use a fastening verb.
The final Hebrew expression is an olive garden; BSB lists vineyards and olive groves separately.
The reply actively says the Timnite took Samson’s wife and gave her to his companion; BSB condenses this to a passive giving. Burning is explicitly “with fire”, without a separate death verb.
The Hebrew begins conditionally, “if you do thus”, and says he will take vengeance and afterward cease; BSB makes the action past and expresses the cessation as not resting until vengeance.
The Hebrew uses the body image “leg upon thigh”; BSB replaces it with “ruthlessly”.
The Hebrew says they spread out “at Lehi”; BSB supplies “the town of” and says “near”.
The Hebrew twice uses going up and speaks of binding Samson; BSB says “attacked”, “come”, and “arrest”.
The Hebrew explicitly says the men went down; BSB supplies “In response” and does not state the downward direction.
The Hebrew names the Philistines’ singular “hand” and asks that the men themselves not fall upon him; BSB omits the hand and explicitly says “kill”.
The Hebrew emphatically states both binding and not killing and repeats “said ... saying”; BSB condenses the speech formula and marks only the binding with “securely”.
The bonds literally “melted” from his hands; BSB has “broke loose”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The first clause is nominal, “a heap, two heaps”; BSB supplies an active “I have piled them into heaps”.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed as “he”; BSB supplies Samson’s name.
The deliverance is given “by the hand of Your servant”, and the uncircumcised have a singular collective “hand”; BSB omits the first hand and pluralizes the second.
His “spirit” returned and he “lived”; BSB has “strength” and the passive “was revived”.
The Hebrew has an implicit “he”; BSB supplies Samson’s name.
